Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

as far as preposition

all the way to a point

also up to, all the way to, down to, all the way from

classical

Cic. Rosc. Com. 20: ab īmīs unguibus ūsque ad verticem summum
Varr. LL 6.34: ūsque ad Decembrem
Traupman 273
Traupman 404

ūsque ad (+ accusative)

ad with the accusative, strengthened by the adverb ūsque

as far as, all the way to; until

All the way to a point in space or time: ūsque ad mare, as far as the sea; ā … ūsque ad, from … to. With names of towns, ūsque with the accusative alone is classical (ūsque Rōmam; Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • tenus (+ ablative) — as far as, up to

    preposition placed after its noun, with the ablative (in verse and Livy also a genitive plural) · also used · classical · Liv. 21.54.9: erat pectoribus tenus aucta; Verg. A. 2.553: capulō tenus (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Ov.; also Liv. and post-Augustan prose)

    Mostly in verse and post-Augustan prose, not in Caesar (Lewis & Short): pectoribus tenus, up to the chest. Verbīs tenus, as far as words go.

Examples

  • nōn ab īmīs unguibus ūsque ad verticem summum … ex fraude, fallāciīs, mendāciīs cōnstāre tōtus vidētur?

    does he not seem, from the tips of his toes to the top of his head, to be made entirely of fraud, tricks and lies?Cic. Rosc. Com. 20

  • dehinc quīntus Quīntīlis et sīc deinceps ūsque ad Decembrem ā numerō

    then the fifth, Quintilis, and so on in order as far as December, named from their numbersVarr. LL 6.34

  • et erat pectoribus tenus aucta nocturnō imbrī

    and it had risen with the night’s rain as far as their chestsLiv. 21.54.9

  • factīs procul, verbīs tenus

    far from it in deeds, as far as words goGell. 17.19.1

  • ūsque ab (+ ablative)

    all the way fromTraupman 404

See also to, from, throughout.
